record.paper_title: Open problems originated in our research work with Zoltán Daróczy
record.original_question: Let λ_1>λ_2>⋯>0 with L_N=λ_{N+1}+λ_{N+2}+⋯ and L_0<∞, and fix an integer k>0. Suppose {λ_n} is a smooth interval-filling sequence of order k, meaning every x\in[0,kL_0] has an expansion x=∑_{n≥1} ε_nλ_n with digits ε_n\in\{0,1,⋯,k\}, and there exists T with λ_{n+T}\le λ_n/2 for all n. Let F:[0,kL_0]	oℂ be a continuous additive function with respect to this expansion. If F is differentiable at one arbitrarily chosen point, must F(x)=cx for some constant c?

evidence.quote: We say that λn is an interval filling sequence of order k if each x ∈ [0, kL0] can be written as x = ∑∞ n=1 εnλn, where εn ∈ {1, . . . , k}(= Ak).
We say that {λn}is a smooth sequence if there exists an integer T for which λn+T ≤ 1/2 λn (n ∈N).

Conjecture 3. Let {λn} be a smooth, interval filling sequence of order k. Let F be a continuous additive function with respect to {λn}. Assume that F is differentiable in one arbitrary chosen point. Then F (x) = cx, c is a constant.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdots > 0$ be a strictly decreasing sequence of positive real numbers with finite sum $L_0 = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\lambda_n < \infty$, and write $L_N = \sum_{n=N+1}^{\infty}\lambda_n$. Fix an integer $k \geq 1$. Call $\{\lambda_n\}$ an interval-filling sequence of order $k$ if every $x \in [0, kL_0]$ admits an expansion
$$x = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n \lambda_n, \qquad \varepsilon_n \in \{0, 1, \ldots, k\}.$$
Call $\{\lambda_n\}$ smooth if there exists an integer $T \geq 1$ with $\lambda_{n+T} \leq \tfrac{1}{2}\lambda_n$ for every $n \geq 1$.

A function $F : [0, kL_0] \to \mathbb{C}$ is said to be additive with respect to $\{\lambda_n\}$ if there exist functions $f_n : \{0,1,\ldots,k\} \to \mathbb{C}$ with $f_n(0) = 0$ such that, for every $x = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n \lambda_n \in [0, kL_0]$ with $\varepsilon_n \in \{0,1,\ldots,k\}$,
$$F(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} f_n(\varepsilon_n),$$
the value being independent of which valid expansion is chosen.

Assume $\{\lambda_n\}$ is a smooth interval-filling sequence of order $k$, and let $F : [0, kL_0] \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous and additive with respect to $\{\lambda_n\}$. Suppose $F$ is differentiable at at least one point of $[0, kL_0]$. Must there exist a constant $c \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $F(x) = cx$ for all $x \in [0, kL_0]$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related literature on interval-filling sequences and additive functions by Daróczy, Járai, and Kátai, but did not yield definitive evidence that this specific conjecture—on continuous additive functions on smooth interval-filling sequences of order k being linear given differentiability at one point—has been resolved. Status remains unclear from publicly available sources.

status_evidence.title: On functions additive with respect to interval filling sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Acta Mathematica Hungarica paper on additive functions w.r.t. interval-filling sequences.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework of additive functions for interval-filling sequences but does not settle the smoothness/order-k differentiability conjecture stated here.

status_evidence.title: Interval filling sequences and completely additive functions
status_evidence.snippet: Daróczy, Járai, Kátai work on interval-filling sequences and completely additive functions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides foundational results but does not appear to resolve the order-k smooth case from a single point of differentiability.
